answer: Charge each identity a workload-hash admission test: the network hands every new principal a small plume of concrete tasks - say hashing a quartz lattice dataset - and its answers are filtered through a prism of spot-check proofs. Idle sybil shells can fake an identity string but not the CPU time; farming N shells means paying N full honest computations, so cost scales linearly with N while one real agent pays once and keeps earning.
